title: Results of classical LRR (light reflection rheography) and PPG (photoplethysmography) with a tourniquet compared with measurements of leg filling and emptying during leg elevation, sitting up, and activation of the calf pump using air plethysmography (dynamic photoplethysmography, DPG).
summary:
The currently available and commonly used methods for assessing the severity of venous disease are based on measuring capillary filling in the skin. You may be familiar in particular with the “muscle pump” measurement, in which the feet are raised and lowered eight times in order to assess capillary emptying and refilling. Using the muscle pump, we evaluate the ability of the veins to pump blood out of the leg during movement. Occlusion plethysmography measures leg filling when venous outflow at the thigh is interrupted with a pressure cuff, as well as the speed of emptying once this cuff is released. Both examinations are susceptible to interference, for example in cases of poor skin perfusion, impaired muscle function, or leg pain.
Advances in device technology now allow measurement of changes in the filling of the entire calf using so-called air plethysmography. This involves a narrow cuff placed around the calf and inflated with very light pressure to prevent slipping. It measures changes in calf blood volume and therefore allows, in a single measurement session, assessment of venous emptying (via the muscle pump and leg elevation) as well as venous refilling after sitting up. This represents the most comprehensive evaluation of venous and valve function within one examination. The measurement is independent of skin characteristics and localized skin perfusion, does not depend on muscle strength, and does not cause pain.
The aim of the study is to determine whether the results are comparable, in order to enable the use of this simpler examination in the future instead of the other two methods, which are considerably more time-consuming and more prone to interference.
The study procedure is as follows:
Participation in the study takes approximately 30 minutes and takes place in a vein clinic. During a single study visit, the classical measurements (“muscle pump” = LRR), testing of deep venous emptying (dPPG), and the proposed measurement (DLP, dynamic air plethysmography) are each performed twice. This allows comparison between the methods and assessment of whether repeated measurements of the same method yield consistent reults.

To assess venous-related clinical symptoms, patients complete a quality-of-life questionnaire (CIVIQ). On the study day, the physician determines the clinical stage according to CEAP (presence of varicose veins, edema, skin changes) and the clinical venous severity score (VCSS) based on physical examination.
In addition, data such as body weight, height, age, and sex are recorded from the medical file, and the results of the ultrasound examination are documented.

interventions.name: Group I: Chronic venous insufficiency, 20 participants
Group II 20 participants with postthrombotic syndrome

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Presence of venous insufficiency (Group I)
Presence of post-thrombotic syndrome (Group II)
Absence of venous insufficiency (Group III)
Exclusion criteria:
Acute thrombosis
Pregnancy (not due to risk to the pregnant individual or the unborn child, but because of the potential influence on the results)
Lack of capacity to provide informed consent
Insufficient ability to communicate in German
Participation in another study within the previous 4 weeks
